title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
abstract: arXiv:2610.23839v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. translated_title: DiscoveryRSI：递归学习以发现有价值的假设
translated_abstract: 科学发现需要将有价值的假设发展为切实可行的研究，然而从这一不断演进的研究过程中学习仍然充满挑战。我们提出了一个关于有价值且可检验的研究假设的操作性定义：即基于证据的、关于重大不确定性的论断，并辅以可行的调查研究、明确的决策标准和替代性解释。我们的 DiscoveryRSI 框架通过多智能体进化搜索构建假设树，将选定的研究编译为可执行的 Harbor 任务，并通过三种机制实现递归学习：假设信用优化将科学评估归因于有记录的研究贡献；测试框架回放识别高效策略与反复出现的失败，以改进研究工作流；再发现机制将已被接受的改进应用于新的研究，为后续学习生成更多经验。我们还引入了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出 DiscoveryRSI 框架，通过多智能体进化搜索构建假设树，并借助假设信用优化、测试框架回放和再发现三种机制，实现对有价值科学假设发现过程的递归式持续学习。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes DiscoveryRSI, a framework that builds hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search and recursively learns to discover valuable scientific hypotheses via three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization, harness replay, and rediscovery.
